literal.prompt: Какая трубка проводит мочу от почки к мочевому пузырю?

literalGroups.primaryGround: NIDDK identifies ureters as thin muscular tubes connecting kidneys and bladder and carrying urine to the bladder (L213-L216). Urethra carries urine out of the body (L219); renal artery brings blood into kidney toward nephrons (retained NIDDK L193-L195); OpenStax states collecting ducts transport nephron-made urine to kidney calyces (L43). Thus only the ureter fits the asked kidney-to-bladder route.
literalGroups.locator: NIDDK Urinary Tract L213-L219; NIDDK Kidneys L193-L195; OpenStax 25.3 L43,L51.

literalGroups.literal: Мочеточники — тонкие мышечные трубки, соединяющие почки с мочевым пузырём и проводящие туда мочу. Поэтому правильный ответ — мочеточник.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NIDDK says ureters are thin tubes of muscle connecting kidneys to bladder and carrying urine there (L216). The explanation states this route and names the keyed structure.

literalGroups.literal: Уретра — трубка у выхода из мочевого пузыря; по ней моча покидает организм при мочеиспускании.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NIDDK explicitly states that the urethra is a tube at the bottom of the bladder through which urine exits during urination.

literalGroups.literal: У человека два мочеточника — тонкие мышечные трубки, соединяющие каждую почку с мочевым пузырём.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NIDDK describes two ureters and calls them thin tubes of muscle connecting the kidneys to bladder; the paired count and muscular construction add a concrete fact beyond the prompt’s route.

literalGroups.literal: Почечная артерия несёт кровь в почку и разветвляется на более мелкие сосуды.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NIDDK states blood flows into the kidney through the renal artery, which branches until blood reaches nephrons; OpenStax describes the branching renal arterial tree.

literalGroups.literal: Собирательные протоки проводят образованную нефронами мочу к чашечкам почки.
literalGroups.primaryGround: OpenStax states renal papillae are bundles of collecting ducts that transport urine made by nephrons to the kidney calyces. This corrects the previous overbroad description of collecting ducts as receiving filtrate directly from nephrons.

absoluteDifficulty.audience: Adult general-knowledge player without specialist urinary anatomy training
absoluteDifficulty.ground: The correct term requires distinguishing ureter from the equally familiar urethra and from kidney structures. The routes make the wrong options reasoned and potentially confusing rather than absurd; recognizing the anatomical pathway is likely for a player familiar with basic human anatomy but is not a broadly universal everyday fact.
